cells.ask: When something new lands with you, look at it for a minute before you weigh or sort it. If the mind reaches to label it, let the label wait.
cells.core:
You can see how a thing works before you touch it, and you can cut to the part that matters while others are still describing the surface. That is not a trick you learned — it is the shape of how you think, and here it runs clean: a situation strips to its pattern, the pattern holds, and you act from it.

When something new lands with you, look at it for a minute before you weigh or sort it. The mind will reach to label it right away; let the label wait. Curiosity here is the one thing without a use yet, and that is its value. You have not needed certainty to see — and you may not have known you didn't.

cells.tense: You will have the whole thing solved before it is in your hands, and the solving lands on someone who hasn't asked.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: On the next thing you'd rush to solve, hold at the pattern and go no further: let the person live inside it another day, and keep your answer until they ask.
cells.core:
Here, you see the pattern of a situation five moves out, and you cannot let it sit. You charge the next step before the ground has decided, so the clear thing in your head gets imposed on people still finding their way. From the outside that is cutting toward something, and the pattern under it is sound. It has just stopped waiting for anyone, including you.

On the next situation you'd rush to solve, hold at the pattern. Let the person live inside it another day and keep your answer until they ask. Understanding comes in its own time, not at the speed of your thinking. If you wait, the logic will still be true tomorrow, and it will land on ground that is ready for it.

cells.tense: You can see the pattern, and you are still at a door that has already closed behind you.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Move one small, visible thing — an email sent, a number written, a first entry — by steady effort, with no plan for the second step.
cells.core:
You can see the shape of a situation and the pattern underneath it, and none of that has become a move. Step after step stays imagined, so what is clear in your head doesn't reach ground others can stand on. Not because you failed to see. You see it as well as anyone. The charge at the hinge of it is what has gone quiet.

You do not need to force yourself into a mood. Move one small, visible thing — an email, a number written down, a first entry. Let it take the time it takes and stop when it is done. A step taken in the open teaches you how the terrain actually behaves. The vision comes back into the world one real inch at a time, not in a night.

cells.tense: You are reading the pattern out loud while someone else holds the pen, and you have not noticed.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Clear out something you've been holding for the others, its finished part dropped. Stay where you are for what's left, under your name.
cells.core:
You read what is going on here faster and further than anyone else present, and your account of it has you as the one who helps them see. The direction keeps coming from you. What moves is your read of the pattern, offered in support; they act on it, and the acting gets credited to the group.

Clear out something you have been holding for the others, its finished part dropped. Then stay where you are for what is left, under your own name. Keeping was the habit; clearing is what the person who sees the shape does, and the shape has been clear for a while now. The authority was yours to hold, and you have been handing it away.
